title: LENTICULAR
description: A full-width claim in Bricolage Grotesque sits over a large lenticular print of Bayyinah TV on a bone ground; the print arrives on its App Store face and settles flat to bayyinahtv.com, with the same headline on both. Beside the print: Bayyinah TV, the two face labels (bayyinahtv.com ⇄ App Store), the fact that the same web app runs on the site and in both store apps, role and years, and three public links.
signature: Type: Bricolage Grotesque 640 (opsz auto) for the claim at 66px (34px on a phone, tracking −0.032em), Public Sans 400/600 for text, Gentrit Technical Mono 13px for years and the 16 → 2 line. Colour: bone ground #f7efea; ink #1f1518 sampled from bayyinahtv.com's own ground; one accent #b41d02 sampled from the site's Start Learning button, job: marks the face a print shows, focus and link hover; the prints carry all other colour, and About sits on the ink. Motion: the tilt — a print turns 14° on its vertical axis on a spring (visualDuration 0.5 s, bounce 0.12, settled by ~0.8 s); the switch sweeps across 4px lenses from the edge that turns away while the lamp's glints slide; the hero does it once on load (App Store face settling to the website); drag release uses spring.snap with the hand's velocity; keyboard and reduced motion jump.
rule: The page is a stack of lenticular prints: each picture holds two real screens of one product, and the angle of the card picks which one you see.
designRead: Reading this as: a frontend and mobile developer for hiring managers and recruiters, leading with Bayyinah TV (one web app that runs on the website and inside both store apps), in a world of lenticular prints where every picture holds two real screens of one product.
hook: The site where every screenshot is a lenticular card: turn the Bayyinah TV one and bayyinahtv.com becomes the App Store page, with the same headline on both.
lead: Bayyinah TV: public and checkable (website, App Store, Google Play), 2023–26, frontend in the core team, and its key fact — the same web app runs on the site and inside both store apps — is exactly a two-face fact for a two-image print.
composition: first-screen.md #3, the claim drawn as a picture: one object holds the web page and the app listing. Claim full width on top; the print large on the left (8 of 12 columns); the project's facts, face labels and links in a narrow right column. Below: a reading block, then rows that alternate print-left / two narrow phone prints / print-right on alternating grounds, a dense index, and About on the ink.

fourAnswers.desktop: who: Gentrit Rashiti (claim and masthead) / what: web and phone apps / for whom: learners, care teams and shoppers / proof: bayyinahtv.com as a real screen at 38% of the first screen, Frontend core team 2023–26, links to the website, App Store and Google Play, Kosovo working remotely
fourAnswers.phone: who: Gentrit Rashiti / what: web and phone apps / for whom: learners, care teams and shoppers / proof: the print at y 250–550 (both faces cropped to the same 'Quran Studies Made Simple' headline at readable size), Frontend core team 2023–26, Website, App Store and Google Play links at the bottom edge of 844

allowed: C17: dev-server LCP (1.5–1.6 s at 4× CPU) is the draft router's two lazy levels; a production build at 4× paints the largest element at 0.82 s (1440) and 0.84 s (390); this page's own code is 9 kB gzip

holdback: Original, 7: the material is real and tied to 'web and phone', but it sits on a familiar skeleton (claim over a screen, facts in a side column, rows, an index, a dark footer), and at rest a still capture shows a screenshot with faint ribs; the lenticular only reads once the card turns.
skillNotes: Helped: (1) M3's test, 'explain the effect in one sentence of engineering', pushed me past a striped CSS overlay to a computed lens: interlaced strips, a 2× cylindrical lens per 4px, the angle from the eye to each lens (tilt plus the lens's offset) picks the strip, so the flip sweeps across the card; and the lamp's glints are a specular term per lens. (2) motion.md's build order (static end state, cause, one token, interruptible, reduced branch, measure, scrub) mapped one-to-one, and the frequency gate settled that keyboard activation jumps. (3) first-screen.md's phone rules (work above 500px, text ≥ 11px in the crop) led to separate phone crops where both faces show the same headline. (4) The checker caught real things: words past the fold (C02), phone targets, a hidden canvas below the fold (M08), the word 'codebase' (T10f). Unclear or wrong: (a) There is no way to capture an interaction-triggered signature moment mid-flight: --frames times from navigation, element screenshots wait for a stable box so they never catch a rotation, and Playwright's fake clock did not drive motion's springs in real proportion. I scrubbed by dragging to fixed angles; the skill should ship '--interact <selector> --frames-after 60,150,300' or document clip screenshots at fixed states. (b) M08 counts an opacity-0 overlay canvas as a 'section that starts invisible' even though the picture under it is visible; a lazily built overlay is not a fade-up. (c) C17 on the required dev server is dominated by the host app's lazy router (two Suspense levels) and the unbundled module graph: 1.6 s dev vs 0.82 s production at 4×; the brief asks for dev + throttle, so every draft will warn; suggest measuring against a production preview or reporting time from the draft's own first paint. (d) Hard rule 9 allows 'one authored figure may build once' while first-screen.md lists 'loader, intro' as costing credibility; it is unclear whether a settle-on-load of the hero work (readable from the first frame) counts as the authored figure or as an intro. I read it as allowed and gated it (reduced motion, late lens, prior touch). (e) 'The claim sets in 2–4 lines at 32–40px' collides with a 15-word claim in a wide grotesque at 358px (5 lines at 34px); say which gives way: words, size or face. (f) The rule 'original or hook ≤ 7 → go back to direct' conflicts with a fixed round of at most two polish passes; there is no step for a re-direct. (g) The checker changed format mid-round (T23 now needs 4+ matches; --list and checks.md appeared later). (h) The tintedGround signal reads body's background; a draft inside a shared shell must restyle body at runtime to get credit. Missing: Crafted-band guidance that the material must read in a still capture (reviewers judge captures first), and a note that a static fallback should match the canvas's rest frame pixel for pixel so the swap does not pop.
